title: pkg/infra structure, wiring, and control flow
answers: How does control flow into pkg/infra services?
How are pkg/infra services wired up?
Which packages run as background services?
body:
pkg/infra/ is Grafana's cross-cutting infra layer (logging, tracing, metrics, caching, locking, kv store, DB facade, HTTP client construction). It is core-only: `.golangci.yml`'s `coreplugins` depguard rule forbids core plugins (testdata, azuremonitor, graphite, cloudwatch) from importing it.
Nearly nothing in pkg/infra self-wires with a local `wire.NewSet` — the only exception is `pkg/infra/metrics/wireset.go:WireSet`. Everything else is wired centrally from `pkg/server/wire_core.go` (e.g. `kvstore.ProvideService`, `tracing.ProvideService` + `wire.Bind(new(tracing.Tracer), ...)`, `remotecache.ProvideService` + bind to `CacheStorage`, `wire.Bind(new(db.DB), new(*sqlstore.SQLStore))`).
Long-running services implement `pkg/registry/registry.go:BackgroundService.Run(ctx) error` and are collected in `pkg/registry/backgroundsvcs/background_services.go:ProvideBackgroundServiceRegistry` — examples: `tracing.TracingService.Run`, `remotecache.RemoteCache.Run`, `metrics/service.go:InternalMetricsService.Run`, `usagestats/service/service.go:UsageStats.Run`, `nats/server.go:Server.Run`.
Logging is consumed via `log.New("name")` for construction and `log.FromContext(ctx)` for request-scoped fields; `tracing.ProvideService` registers a contextual log provider that injects `traceID` into every `FromContext` call.
Note: `bus`, `cache`, `registry`, `appcontext`, `grpcutil`, `plugins/repo` are NOT under pkg/infra — `registry.BackgroundService` actually lives in `pkg/registry/registry.go`; caching is split into `localcache` (in-process) and `remotecache` (distributed).
